sentence: This project builds an open-source platform that integrates computational and experimental technologies to help discover peptide therapeutics for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.
This project studies how exposure to perfluorooctane sulfonate impairs pancreatic beta cell function and mitochondrial mechanisms and contributes to gestational diabetes.
This project builds computational and experimental technologies to speed up the discovery of narrow-spectrum antibiotics for Lyme disease.
This project studies post-transcriptional regulation of key metabolic genes to understand how the body maintains systemic metabolism.
This project tests whether a neuromarker predicts craving and distinguishes drug users from non-users, and studies its underlying neurobiological ingredients.
This project studies how chemical exposures and inherited cancer susceptibility genes shape tumor initiation, promotion and progression in the mouse.
This project develops accurate assays that measure viral susceptibility of HIV to broadly neutralizing antibodies at the point-of-care with fast turnaround.
This project studies the molecular mechanisms that control telomere length and how telomerase maintains telomeres.
This project studies how cellular senescence changes and differs across bone marrow, breast, colon and liver tissue.
This project studies how thinking about an emotional stimulus in a more adaptive way changes health-related behavior in unpaid caregivers of persons with Alzheimer’s Disease.
This project brings together basic, clinical and population research to reduce how often cancer occurs and how many people die from it.
This project studies how cholinergic signaling changes amygdalar circuits to regulate emotional memory at the cellular and circuit level.
This project studies how biliary fibrosis progresses and tests the safety and short-term effect of a treatment in children with cholestatic liver disease.
This project uses positron emission tomography brain imaging to study how manganese causes degeneration of the dopaminergic system and whether neuroinflammation plays a part.
This project looks for biomarkers of tumor burden in neurofibroma using plasma from mice, human patient samples and mass spectrometry.
This project develops gene editing strategies to correct mutations in a gap junction gene that cause the most common hereditary deafness.
This project uses biochemical and cellular assays to find how non-coding mutations affect gene regulation by cardiac transcription factors in congenital heart defects.
This project provides next-generation sequencing and bioinformatics analysis services to support genomic research on diabetes.
This project uses genetics and neuropsychology to study why alcohol use problems and suicidal thoughts and behaviors occur together in adolescents and clinical samples.
This project finds and studies unknown immune systems in staphylococci against the viruses that infect them, and how these defenses spread.
